# FDG8020

> DO NOT provide settable collection properties.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.2 Collection Properties and Return Values.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA2227
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Test profile: test classes are public only for the test framework; their signatures are not API. CA2227 reports an externally visible property with a public setter whose type is a writable collection (Collection<T>, IList<T>, Dictionary<TKey, TValue> in a probe with SDK 10.0.402). It does not report an array (CA1819, FDG8003), a ReadOnlyCollection<T>, IReadOnlyList<T> or IEnumerable<T> property, a private setter or an init accessor, so coverage is partial. Removing a public setter changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA2227 has no code fix.

## From the book

Users can replace the contents of the collection by clearing the collection first and then adding the new contents. If replacing the whole collection is a common scenario, consider providing the `AddRange` method on the collection.

```csharp
// bad design
public class Order {
   public Collection<OrderItem> Items { get { ... } set { ... } }
   ...
}
// good design
public class Order {
   public Collection<OrderItem> Items { get { ... } }
   ...
}
```
